claims.text: The target domain is multicomponent high-entropy alloys containing up to five principal elements at temperatures near fusion.
Accurate treatment near fusion requires both solid and liquid free energies, including detailed entropy contributions.
The proposed intervention is to embed an ML free-energy correction surrogate within TOR-TILD.
The ML surrogates will be trained on high-fidelity ab initio free-energy data from elemental and binary systems.
Surrogate free-energy corrections will allow most molecular-dynamics evaluations to be bypassed.
An ML model trained on first-principles data can predict relevant quantities for high-entropy-alloy systems.
Training on simpler elemental and binary systems will transfer sufficiently well to predict subtle free-energy corrections in multicomponent alloys.
The surrogate will accurately retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling contributions.
Replacing most molecular-dynamics steps with surrogate corrections will preserve the fidelity of the free-energy landscape.
The ML-augmented workflow will predict phase free energies and derived observables with less than approximately 5% deviation from full ab initio molecular dynamics.
The ML-augmented workflow will be approximately 5–10 times faster than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The ML-augmented workflow will be approximately 2–3 times faster than standard TOR-TILD.
Explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and standard TOR-TILD require substantially more molecular-dynamics sampling time, particularly for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The method will remain reliable for alloys with up to five principal elements near their melting temperatures.
Performance outside the calibration temperature range or for systems with more than five principal elements is uncertain.
Success in multicomponent alloys depends on the quality and transferability of training data obtained from simpler systems.
